chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qazwini, Abu'l-Hasan, known as Ibn Maqbara, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Amir narrated to us. He said: Isam ibn Yusuf narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Kilabi narrated to us. He said: Amr ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thabit. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever loves Ali in his life and after his death, God, Mighty and Majestic, shall write for him security and faith equivalent to all that the sun rises and sets upon. And whoever hates him in his life and after his death shall die the death of jahiliyya and be held accountable for what he did.

key_terms.أبغضه: Hatred/enmity — a strong term denoting active hostility, not mere indifference
key_terms.الأمن والإيمان: Security and faith — the two supreme blessings, covering both worldly safety and spiritual well-being
key_terms.ميتة جاهلية: Death of jahiliyya — dying in a state of pre-Islamic ignorance, outside the fold of true Islam

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about loving and hating Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a mixed Sunni-Shia chain reaching back to the Companion Zayd ibn Thabit, records the Prophet declaring eternal divine reward for those who love Imam Ali (AS) — both during Ali's lifetime and after his martyrdom in 40 AH. The promise of 'security and faith' spanning all that the sun touches uses a classical Arabic expression for total, universal scope. Conversely, dying the 'death of jahiliyya' — the pre-Islamic age of ignorance — is among the gravest warnings in prophetic speech, indicating death outside the bounds of true faith and community.
